course.subtitle: Build your own Shopify store with AI in 7 live classes.

By Day 7 your store has real products, payments switched on, and a design that works on mobile, ready to take its first order.

module.title: Start here
module.summary: Welcome class: how the 7 days work, what you need, and how to get help.

content.notes:
WELCOME TO THE 7-DAY STARTER
In 7 live classes you will build your own Shopify store with AI: niche, product, store, design, payments, delivery and launch.

HOW IT WORKS
- Live class every day at 9 PM IST on Google Meet, about 1 hour. Day 1 is Mon 2 Nov, Day 7 is Sun 8 Nov.
- Each day has notes, AI prompts, a step-by-step PDF guide and a small homework task here in the app.
- Submit homework under each day. Roshan checks it and gives feedback.
- Missed a class? The recording link is on that day's page.

WHAT YOU NEED
- A laptop or phone with Chrome, a Gmail account, and WhatsApp.
- A free AI account: ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude.
- Optional: an idea of what you'd like to sell.

FEES
₹999 in total: ₹499 to join, and ₹500 before Day 3 (Wed 4 Nov). Classes from Day 3 stay locked until the balance is paid.

ഓരോ ദിവസവും ക്ലാസ് കഴിഞ്ഞ് homework ഇവിടെ submit ചെയ്യൂ. സംശയം വന്നാൽ WhatsApp-ൽ ചോദിക്കാം.

Doubts? WhatsApp Roshan: +91 70120 45854
content.assign_text: Introduce yourself: your name, your town, and what you'd like to sell online (even a rough idea is fine). If you already sell something, tell us what.

module.title: Find and check (Day 1 to 2)
module.summary: Choose one clear niche and a hero product that really makes a profit.

lesson.title: Day 1 · Find Your Niche with AI

content.notes:
BY THE END OF TODAY
- You understand how an online store makes money, from the first post to the delivered parcel.
- You have used AI to brainstorm at least 20 niche ideas that fit you.
- You have checked your top ideas with free research tools (Google Trends, Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, Instagram).
- You have chosen one niche and written a one-line brand angle for it.

THE BIG IDEA
Most first-time sellers fail for one simple reason: they try to sell everything to everyone. A store that sells phone covers, sarees, perfume and toys looks like a random shop, and nobody trusts it.

എല്ലാവർക്കും വേണ്ടി വിൽക്കാൻ ശ്രമിച്ചാൽ ആരും വാങ്ങില്ല. ഒരു ചെറിയ കൂട്ടം ആളുകളെ മനസ്സിൽ കണ്ടു തുടങ്ങൂ.

AI PROMPTS FOR TODAY (copy into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, and fill the [brackets])

▸ Prompt 1.1 · Niche brainstorm
Using what you know about me, suggest 20 specific niche ideas for a first Shopify store in India.
My skills and interests: [list]
People I know well: [list]
Products I can get easily: [list]
Budget for first stock: [₹ amount]

For each idea give:
1. The niche in one line (product + exact buyer)
2. The main problem or wish it solves
3. A rough selling price range in ₹
4. Why it could work in Kerala or India right now

Avoid very big, crowded markets like "mobile accessories" or "general clothing". Avoid products that need special licences, are fragile, or are banned for online sale.

▸ Prompt 1.2 · Go deeper on 5 ideas
Here are my 5 favourite niche ideas: [paste them].
For each one, tell me:
- Who exactly is the buyer (age, gender, city type, income, what they do)
- Where these buyers spend time online (Instagram pages, YouTube channels, WhatsApp or Facebook groups)
- What they search for on Google or Amazon (5 example search phrases)
- The top 3 worries they have before buying online
- One thing a small new brand could do better than big brands
Then rank the 5 ideas from best to worst for a beginner with my budget, and explain why in one line each.

▸ Prompt 1.3 · Competitor gap finder
I want to sell [product] to [buyer] in India. Here are the main complaints I found in 1-star and 2-star reviews of competing products: [paste 5 to 10 complaints].
Here is what small Instagram brands in this niche are doing: [short notes].
1. Group the complaints into 3 to 5 main problems.
2. For each problem, suggest a simple way my new brand can fix it or promise it.
3. Suggest 3 possible "brand angles" (one sentence each) that make my store feel different.

▸ Prompt 1.4 · Brand angle and customer card
My niche: I help [who] get [result] with [product].
1. Write 5 short brand angle options (under 12 words each) that a small Kerala brand could own.
2. Create a one-page "customer card" for my ideal buyer: name, age, city, job, monthly income, daily routine, where they shop online, what makes them trust a new store, what stops them from buying, and the exact words they might use to describe their problem.
3. Suggest 10 simple brand name ideas that are easy to say in Malayalam and English, 2 to 3 syllables, and likely available as a .in domain. Do not use existing big brand names.

Full step-by-step guide: open the PDF below. Doubts? WhatsApp Roshan: +91 70120 45854
content.assign_text:
Homework for today:

1. Finish your niche card: the "I help..." sentence, brand angle, customer card, and 3 brand name options.
2. Talk to 3 real people who fit your buyer (WhatsApp is fine). Ask: "Would you buy [product] online? What would you pay? What would stop you?" Write their answers down.
3. Save at least 10 screenshots in your swipe file.
4. Bring your niche card to Class 2. We will turn it into a product shortlist and check the profit.

Submit here: write what you did, paste a link (Google Doc, Canva, store link) or upload a photo / screenshot.

lesson.title: Day 2 · Pick and Check Your Product

content.notes:
BY THE END OF TODAY
- You have a shortlist of 10 product ideas inside your niche, made with AI.
- You have checked real demand for your best 5 ideas.
- You know where to buy or make your product, and what one piece really costs.
- You have done the full margin check and picked one hero product (plus 2 to 3 backups) at a price that leaves real profit.

THE BIG IDEA
Yesterday you chose who you sell to. Today you choose what you sell, and you make sure it can actually make money.

വില ഇടുന്നതിനു മുമ്പ് എല്ലാ ചെലവും കൂട്ടി നോക്കൂ. Shipping, packing, ads, return എല്ലാം ചേർത്താലാണ് ശരിയായ ലാഭം അറിയുന്നത്.

AI PROMPTS FOR TODAY (copy into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, and fill the [brackets])

▸ Prompt 2.1 · 10 product ideas in my niche
My niche: I help [who] get [result] with [product type].
My customer card: [paste a short version].
My budget for first stock: [₹ amount].
Suggest 10 specific products I could sell first. For each product give:
- Product name and a one-line description
- Typical selling price in India (₹)
- Rough cost to buy or make one piece (₹), and where I could source it in India
- Weight and size when packed (light, medium, heavy)
- Risk level for a beginner (low, medium, high) and why
Prefer products that are light, not fragile, easy to photograph, and can sell for at least 3 times their cost.

▸ Prompt 2.2 · Supplier questions
I want to buy [product] from a supplier in India to sell online. Write a short, polite WhatsApp message I can send to suppliers asking for:
- price per piece for 10, 25 and 50 pieces
- available sizes and colours
- whether they can send 1 or 2 samples first, and the cost
- how many days to dispatch, and who pays transport
- whether they allow exchange for damaged pieces
Also give me a list of 8 questions to ask on a phone call to judge if the supplier is reliable.
Write it in simple English and also in Malayalam.

▸ Prompt 2.3 · Margin check and price advice
Help me check the profit on my product. Show the calculation as a simple table.
Product: [name]
Selling price I am thinking of: ₹[A]
Product cost: ₹[B]
Packing: ₹[C]
Shipping per order: ₹[D]
Payment gateway fee: 2% + 18% GST on the fee
Marketing per order: ₹[F]
Returns buffer: 5% of the price
1. Calculate my profit per order and margin %.
2. If margin is below 25%, suggest 3 ways to fix it (higher price, bundles, cheaper packing, a different supplier, minimum order value for free shipping).
3. Suggest a "compare-at" (MRP) price that is honest and believable.
4. Suggest one bundle offer that increases the average order value.

▸ Prompt 2.4 · Hero product summary
Here is my final product decision: [paste your table].
1. Point out any risks I may have missed (shipping, returns, sizes, seasons, competition).
2. Suggest 3 product name ideas for my hero product that are clear and searchable (include the product type, material and main benefit).
3. List the 6 photos I should take of this product for my store.
4. List the top 5 questions buyers will ask before buying, so I can answer them on the product page.

Full step-by-step guide: open the PDF below. Doubts? WhatsApp Roshan: +91 70120 45854
content.assign_text:
Homework for today:

1. Get a sample of your hero product in hand (or a confirmed date for it). If you make it yourself, make one finished piece.
2. Finish your hero product table and the margin calculator.
3. Keep these ready for Class 3 (we create your store and payments tomorrow): PAN, bank account number and IFSC, your phone with Aadhaar OTP, a debit or credit card for online payments, and your 3 brand name options.
4. If you joined with ₹499, pay the remaining ₹500 before Class 3 starts (Wed 4 Nov, 9 PM) so Day 3 opens for you in the app.

Submit here: write what you did, paste a link (Google Doc, Canva, store link) or upload a photo / screenshot.

module.title: Build your store (Day 3 to 6)
module.summary: Create the Shopify store, add products with AI, design it, and make it ready to take orders.

lesson.title: Day 3 · Set Up Shopify, Domain and Payments

content.notes:
BY THE END OF TODAY
- Your Shopify store is created and the basic store details are filled in.
- You know your way around the Shopify admin.
- Your domain (yourbrand.in or .com) is bought or connected.
- Razorpay is signed up, KYC is submitted, and UPI and card payments plus Cash on Delivery are set up.
- Your shipping rates are set, including a free-shipping offer.

THE BIG IDEA
Today your idea becomes a real place on the internet. Think of Shopify as renting a ready-made shop in a mall: the building, security, billing counter and lights are all done. You just put your name on the board, arrange your products and open the doors.

ഇന്ന് design-നെ കുറിച്ച് വിഷമിക്കേണ്ട. ആദ്യം Store-ന്റെ അടിസ്ഥാനം ശരിയാക്കാം: Domain, Payment, Shipping.

AI PROMPTS FOR TODAY (copy into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, and fill the [brackets])

▸ Prompt 3.1 · Domain name ideas
My brand name ideas are: [list]. My niche: [one line].
Suggest 15 domain name options using these names, ending in .in or .com. Keep them short (under 15 letters), easy to spell for Malayalis and other Indians, and with no hyphens or numbers.
For each, show it as name.in and name.com. Mark your top 3 and say why.

Full step-by-step guide: open the PDF below. Doubts? WhatsApp Roshan: +91 70120 45854
content.assign_text:
Homework for today:

1. Finish any step above that you could not finish in class.
2. Check your email and WhatsApp for Razorpay activation. If they ask for more documents, send them the same day.
3. Take your product photos tonight or tomorrow morning in daylight (see the photo guide in Class 4 if you want a head start). You need at least 4 photos of your hero product.
4. Write down for each product: price, compare-at price, cost, sizes or colours, weight with packing.

Submit here: write what you did, paste a link (Google Doc, Canva, store link) or upload a photo / screenshot.

content.notes:
BY THE END OF TODAY
- You know what makes a product page sell, and what makes people leave.
- You have taken (or improved) clear product photos with your phone.
- You have used AI to write your product title, description, FAQ and search listing.
- Your hero product and 2 to 3 backups are added, priced and set to Active in Shopify, inside a collection.

THE BIG IDEA
Your product page is your salesperson. In a real shop, a buyer can touch the fabric, ask questions and try a size. Online, the page must do all of that with photos and a few clear lines.

Product page ഒരു salesman പോലെയാണ്. ഫോട്ടോ, വില, delivery, return എല്ലാം വ്യക്തമായി കാണിക്കണം.

AI PROMPTS FOR TODAY (copy into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, and fill the [brackets])

▸ Prompt 4.1 · Full product page
Write the product page content for my Shopify store.
Brand: [name]. Brand angle: [one line]. Buyer: [customer card summary].
Product facts: [paste your table].
Write in simple, warm English that a Kerala buyer understands easily. No fancy words. No made-up claims.
Give me:
1. Product title (under 70 characters): product type + key feature + colour/size if useful
2. A one-line hook (under 20 words) for the top of the description
3. Description: a short paragraph (3 lines) about the feeling or result, then 5 bullet points (benefit first, then the fact), then a "Perfect for" line
4. A "Details" section: material, size or weight, what's included, care instructions
5. A "Delivery and returns" section using my rules
6. 5 FAQs buyers in India would ask, with short answers
7. SEO page title (under 60 characters) and meta description (under 155 characters)
8. Alt text for each of my 6 photos: [list them]

▸ Prompt 4.2 · Make it sound like me
Here is the description you wrote: [paste].
Rewrite it so it sounds like a friendly small Kerala brand owner talking to a customer on WhatsApp. Keep it under 150 words. Keep the 5 bullet points. Add one short line in Malayalam at the end that feels warm and personal.

▸ Prompt 4.3 · Collection and store copy
My products are: [list with one line each]. My brand angle: [line].
1. Suggest 3 collection names and a one-line description for each.
2. Write a short "Why buy from us" list with 3 points (under 8 words each) for my product pages.
3. Write a short size guide or usage guide for [product], as a simple table.

Full step-by-step guide: open the PDF below. Doubts? WhatsApp Roshan: +91 70120 45854
content.assign_text:
Homework for today:

1. Finish adding all your products (hero plus 2 to 3 backups) with photos and checked text.
2. Open every product page on your phone and fix anything hard to read.
3. Make or choose your logo for Class 5. A simple text logo is fine (you can make one free in Canva). Save it as a PNG with a transparent background, about 1000 px wide.
4. Pick 2 brand colours and save 3 home pages you like from your swipe file.

Submit here: write what you did, paste a link (Google Doc, Canva, store link) or upload a photo / screenshot.

lesson.title: Day 5 · Design That Looks Like a Brand

content.notes:
BY THE END OF TODAY
- You have a simple brand kit: logo, 2 colours, 1 or 2 fonts, and a tone of voice.
- You have chosen a free Shopify theme and set your logo, colours and fonts in Theme settings.
- Your home page is built section by section, with text written with AI.
- Your menus (header and footer) are set, and every page looks good on a phone.

THE BIG IDEA
People decide whether to trust a new store in a few seconds, mostly from how it looks. A clean, consistent store feels like a real brand. A messy one feels like a scam, even when the product is great.

Design ലളിതമായി വെക്കൂ. രണ്ട് നിറം, ഒരു font, നല്ല ഫോട്ടോകൾ. അത്രയും മതി ഒരു Brand പോലെ തോന്നാൻ.

AI PROMPTS FOR TODAY (copy into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, and fill the [brackets])

▸ Prompt 5.1 · Brand kit
My brand: [name]. Niche: [line]. Brand angle: [line]. Buyer: [short customer card].
Create a simple brand kit for my Shopify store:
1. Brand personality in 3 words
2. A colour palette: 1 main colour, 1 accent colour, 1 background colour and 1 text colour, each as a hex code, with a reason. Make sure text is easy to read on the background.
3. Two font pairings available in Shopify themes (one for headings, one for body text). Prefer clean, readable fonts.
4. Tone of voice: 5 do's and 5 don'ts for how my brand writes, with example sentences
5. A short tagline (under 8 words) in English, and one in Malayalam

▸ Prompt 5.2 · Home page copy
Write home page text for my Shopify store. Keep everything short and easy to read on a phone.
Brand: [name]. Tagline: [line]. Buyer: [line]. Hero product: [line]. Offer: [free shipping above ₹___, COD available, etc.]
1. Announcement bar: 3 options (under 60 characters)
2. Hero banner: a headline (under 8 words), a sub-headline (under 18 words), and button text (2 to 3 words)
3. Featured collection heading (under 5 words)
4. "Why choose us": 3 points, each with a 3-word title and a 10-word line
5. "Our story": 3 short sentences about who we are and why we started
6. FAQ: 6 questions and short answers about delivery time, COD, returns, sizes, payment safety, and contact
7. Footer: a one-line brand description and a newsletter line
Keep the tone: [your 3 personality words].

▸ Prompt 5.3 · Design review
I am sharing a screenshot of my Shopify store home page on mobile. [attach screenshot]
Review it like an e-commerce designer for Indian shoppers. Tell me:
1. The 3 biggest problems that might stop someone from buying
2. Whether the headline, price and buy button are clear
3. Whether the colours and fonts look consistent and readable
4. 5 small, specific fixes I can make in the Shopify theme editor today

Full step-by-step guide: open the PDF below. Doubts? WhatsApp Roshan: +91 70120 45854
content.assign_text:
Homework for today:

1. Finish your home page and product page, and ask 2 friends to open your store on their phones. Ask: "What do we sell? Would you trust it? What confused you?"
2. Write down your return and exchange rules (how many days, who pays return shipping, what can't be returned). We use them in Class 6.
3. Write 3 to 5 lines about your story: who you are, why you started, what makes your product special.

Submit here: write what you did, paste a link (Google Doc, Canva, store link) or upload a photo / screenshot.

lesson.title: Day 6 · Trust Pages and a Test Order

content.notes:
BY THE END OF TODAY
- Your About, Contact and FAQ pages are live and sound like you.
- Your five policies (refund, privacy, terms, shipping, contact) are clear, true and linked in the footer.
- Your order emails and checkout look right and carry your brand.
- You have placed one full test order, seen it arrive in Orders, and cancelled it.
- Shiprocket (or your courier) is connected, so you know exactly how a real order gets packed and shipped.

THE BIG IDEA
A new store is a stranger. Before someone pays a stranger, they look for signs that it is safe: a real person behind it, a phone number, a clear return rule, and a checkout that works. Today we add all those signs, and then we test the whole buying journey ourselves, so our first real customer never finds a broken step.

Customer-ന് വിശ്വാസം വന്നാലേ പണം അടയ്ക്കൂ. നിങ്ങളുടെ പേര്, ഫോൺ നമ്പർ, Return നിയമം എല്ലാം വ്യക്തമായി കാണിക്കൂ.

AI PROMPTS FOR TODAY (copy into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, and fill the [brackets])

▸ Prompt 6.1 · About page
Write an "About us" page for my Shopify store. Keep it under 200 words, warm and honest.
My name: [name]. Where I am: [town, Kerala].
Why I started: [your 3 to 5 lines from homework].
What makes my product special: [facts only].
Who it is for: [buyer].
Structure: a headline, a short opening line, 2 short paragraphs, and 3 bullet "promises" (for example: real photos, fast replies on WhatsApp, easy exchange). End with an invitation to message us.
Add one warm closing line in Malayalam.

▸ Prompt 6.2 · Refund and shipping policies
Write two clear, simple policies for my small online store in India. Use headings and short points, not legal jargon.
Store name: [name]. Contact: [WhatsApp, email, address].
My rules: [paste your table].
1. Refund and exchange policy
2. Shipping and delivery policy (include dispatch time, delivery time, charges, free-shipping threshold, COD, what happens if a parcel is refused or the address is wrong, tracking)
Also include a "Grievance / complaints contact" section with my name, email and phone, and say we reply within 48 hours.

▸ Prompt 6.3 · Review my privacy policy and terms
Here are the privacy policy and terms of service that Shopify created from its template for my store: [paste].
My store is a small business in [town], Kerala, India, selling [products]. We collect name, phone, email and address for delivery, and use Razorpay for payments and [Shiprocket / courier] for shipping.
1. Point out anything that doesn't fit an Indian small business.
2. Suggest simple wording changes, keeping the meaning legally safe.
3. Remind me of anything I should check with a lawyer or CA.

Full step-by-step guide: open the PDF below. Doubts? WhatsApp Roshan: +91 70120 45854

module.title: Launch (Day 7)
module.summary: Final checklist, go live, and get your first customers on Instagram and WhatsApp.

lesson.title: Day 7 · Launch Checklist and First Customers

content.notes:
BY THE END OF TODAY
- You have gone through the full launch checklist and fixed anything missing.
- Your store password is off: the store is open to the public.
- Your Instagram profile is ready and your first 3 posts are planned (and post 1 is live).
- You have a launch-day message ready for WhatsApp, a launch discount code, and a list of people to send it to.
- You know which numbers to watch each day, and what to do in your first 30 days.

THE BIG IDEA
A store doesn't sell just because it is open. Nobody knows it exists yet. Your first customers will almost always come from people who already know you: friends, family, colleagues, your local area, and their friends. Big ads come later, once you know your product sells.

ആദ്യ ഓർഡറുകൾ വരുന്നത് നിങ്ങളെ അറിയാവുന്നവരിൽ നിന്നാണ്. Ads-ന് പണം കളയുന്നതിനു മുമ്പ് സുഹൃത്തുക്കളോടും കുടുംബത്തോടും പറയൂ.

AI PROMPTS FOR TODAY (copy into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, and fill the [brackets])

▸ Prompt 7.1 · Last-minute store review
I am launching my Shopify store today. Here is my store link: [link]. (If your AI tool can't open links, paste the text of your home page and hero product page instead.)
Act like a first-time buyer from Kerala who has never heard of my brand.
1. What would make you trust this store, and what would make you leave?
2. Is anything confusing about price, delivery, COD or returns?
3. List any spelling mistakes or unclear sentences you notice.
4. Give me the 5 most important fixes, in order.

▸ Prompt 7.2 · Instagram bio
Write 5 Instagram bio options for my store (each under 150 characters, using line breaks and 1 or 2 emojis).
Brand: [name]. Buyer: [line]. Product: [line]. Trust points: [COD, free shipping above ₹___, made in Kerala...].
End each with a call to action that points to the link.
Add one Malayalam-English mixed version.

▸ Prompt 7.3 · 3 launch posts
Plan my first 3 Instagram posts for the launch of my store.
Brand: [name]. Brand angle: [line]. Buyer: [line]. Hero product: [line, price]. Offer: [code LAUNCH10, 7 days].
For each post give me:
1. The format (photo, carousel or Reel) and exactly what to shoot on my phone
2. Text to put on the image (under 8 words)
3. The caption: a strong first line, 3 short lines, a call to action, in simple English with a little Malayalam mixed in
4. 10 hashtags (mix of Kerala, India and niche hashtags)
For the Reel, give me a 15-second script with 4 shots and an on-screen hook for the first 2 seconds.

▸ Prompt 7.4 · Launch message
Write a short, personal WhatsApp message announcing my new online store to friends and family. It should not sound like spam.
My name: [name]. Brand: [name]. What I sell: [line]. Why I started: [one line]. Link: [store link]. Offer: code LAUNCH10 for 10% off until [date].
Give me 3 versions: (1) English, (2) Malayalam, (3) Malayalam-English mixed. Each under 70 words. End with a soft ask, like sharing it with one person who would like it.

Full step-by-step guide: open the PDF below. Doubts? WhatsApp Roshan: +91 70120 45854
content.assign_text:
Homework for today:

Your homework is now your business.

1. Send your launch message to your full list of 30 people over the next 2 days.
2. Post on Instagram or WhatsApp Status every day for the next 14 days (use the 30-day plan at the end of this book).
3. Pack and ship every order within 1 to 2 days, and ask every buyer for a review.
4. Every Sunday, write down: visits, orders, revenue, profit, and one thing to improve next week.
5. Message +91 70120 45854 when you get your first order. We want to celebrate it with you! 🎉

Submit here: write what you did, paste a link (Google Doc, Canva, store link) or upload a photo / screenshot.
